topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the scope of the lecture series, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causes and carcinogen evaluation.

topics.label: Foundations of Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Environment, and Chance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the fundamental drivers of cancer development, examining the interplay among endogenous cellular errors, inherited genetic predispositions, and environmental exposures.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Viral Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents promote cancer, using the relationship between Epstein-Barr virus, malaria, and Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how diverse chemical and physical agents undergo metabolic processing and directly or indirectly cause DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor Initiation and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate the two-stage model of carcinogenesis by distinguishing direct DNA-damaging initiators from non-mutagenic, inflammation-driven promoters.

topics.label: Host Tissue Context and Developmental Timing in Cancer Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how an individual's life stage, tissue proliferation status, and developmental windows alter susceptibility to carcinogenic insults.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Evaluating Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the experimental, epidemiological, genomic, and risk-assessment strategies used to determine and measure carcinogenicity.
